Definition: Integration of company registration, business licensing, tax compliance, regulatory compliance data
Comments: Center for Formalization of Businesses (CFE, one-stop shop) was established but support is waning. No e-commerce or e-signature law exists. Business registration is partially digitized but not integrated with tax, ID, or other registries. ENTD.GW plans to strengthen digital business services.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original 2023 World Bank source confirmed as related and still broadly valid, but corroborating checks found the CFE one-stop-shop platform (cfe.gw, accessed 2026) now describes an automatic data handoff to the tax authority (DGCI) for NIF assignment on company registration — a bilateral link beyond mere 'planning'. However, a World Bank-funded WARDIP feasibility study for a national interoperability framework/data exchange layer for Guinea-Bissau (devemerge.com tender, 2024/25) shows the actual exchange platform is still at the design/feasibility stage, not yet built. No evidence of integration with ID, land or other registries. Recalculated from 'Planned' (2) to 'Under development' (3): concrete point-to-point automation exists and a formal interoperability build is underway, but full data-exchange integration is not yet operational.

Definition: Integration of tax administration and revenue collection systems data into the exchange platform
Comments: Kontaktu (homegrown tax declaration/filing/payment system) is operational but operates as an isolated system. SIGFIP (financial management) is partially adopted but not uniformly. No documented API-level integration between tax system and other government registries.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: IMF Guinea-Bissau Selected Issues report (June 2025) confirms Kontaktu (e-filing/payment) remains operational but its integration potential is 'hindered by low capacity' and it is not described as linked to other government systems — consistent with the original 'isolated system' assessment. A World Bank-funded WARDIP feasibility study for an interoperability framework/data exchange layer (devemerge.com, 2024/25) shows Guinea-Bissau has moved from mere planning into active design work on the exchange platform, though it is not yet operational. Recalculated from 'Planned' (2) to 'Under development' (3) on this basis; still no evidence of API-level integration with other registries, so not scored higher.
